input: nums is an Array of n positive integers in [1,1000000], with 0 <= n <= 10000. Inputs with fewer than three entries are an explicit extension. Integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, subclasses, proxies or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The largest perimeter of any nondegenerate triangle formed from three distinct input occurrences, or 0 if none exists. Equal-valued occurrences may be used separately; a zero-area triangle is not valid.
mutation_aliasing: Only a fresh copy is sorted; caller values and ordering remain unchanged. No triangle or mutated array is returned. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Every pair sum is at most 2000000 and every three-side perimeter at most 3000000. Comparator differences are within [-999999,999999]. Indices and all arithmetic intermediates are exact safe integers.
complexity: After sorting, O(n+1) descending work checks consecutive triples from the largest side down. If its two largest possible smaller sides fail the strict triangle inequality, no triangle with that largest side can succeed; the first success maximizes perimeter. JavaScript copied sorting adds O(n+1) copying plus target-runtime T_sort(n) comparison/sort work and S_sort(n) workspace. ECMAScript supplies no universal O(n log n) sort complexity guarantee; comparator work is bounded O(1) here and is included in T_sort.
